text:
Toronto led 3-0 after nine minutes and still lost, which says more about the next 50 minutes than the first ten. The Maple Leafs scored on shots that gave them roughly a 4, 21 and 19 percent chance apiece, through Jack Roslovic, Easton Cowan and Nick Paul, and then Vegas started playing the game it had been playing all along. Mark Stone cut it to 3-1 late in the first, Brett Howden deflected in a second-period goal, and Jack Eichel tied it at 3-3 less than four minutes after that.

From there the chances were lopsided. Vegas piled up 83 shot attempts to Toronto's 54 and 4.99 expected goals to 2.60, and 2.12 of those came in the second period alone. Eichel logged 26:36 and put six shots on goal, and the sequence of Stone, Howden and Eichel scoring in succession was the product of sustained pressure. By the numbers, Vegas won 82 percent of simulated replays of every shot. Sergei Bobrovsky faced 43 shots and stopped about two goals more than expected, which is the only reason Toronto reached overtime with a point at stake.

The shootout was close to a wash. Braeden Bowman and Kirill Marchenko traded goals, then Eichel, Auston Matthews, Shea Theodore, William Nylander, Mitch Marner and Gavin McKenna were all stopped. Trevor Connelly beat Bobrovsky with a backhand in the fifth round, and John Tavares was denied to end it. Vegas won 4-3, and for once the result matched the way the game was played.
